title: Rigveda 9.52: To Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 9.52: To Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 9.52 is a hymn of 5 verses addressed to Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 9, the hymns to Soma Pavamāna. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 686v-687r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 9.52.1-2 (aṣṭaka 7, adhyāya 1, varga 9); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 686v
translation.original_text:
1pari̍ dyu̱kṣaḥ sa̱nadra̍yi̱r bhara̱d vāja̍ṁ no̱ andha̍sā | su̱vā̱no a̍rṣa pa̱vitra̱ ā ||
2tava̍ pra̱tnebhi̱r adhva̍bhi̱r avyo̱ vāre̱ pari̍ pri̱yaḥ | sa̱hasra̍dhāro yā̱t tanā̍ ||
translation.text:
1WEALTH-WINNER, dwelling in the sky, bringing us vigour with the juice, Flow to the filter when effused.
2So, in thine ancient ways, may he, beloved, with a thousand streams Run o'er the fleecy straining-cloth.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 686v (numbered 3v by the scribe) (OPenn image 687, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.50.3 ‹-harim hinvanti adri-bhiḥ pavamānam›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 687r (numbered 4r by the scribe), begins in RV 9.52.3 ‹-itivadha-sno īṅkhaya›. Verses 9.52.1-2 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1pari | dyukṣaḥ | sanat-rayiḥ | bharat | vājam | naḥ | andhasā | suvānaḥ | aṣar | pavitre | ā
2tava | pratnebhiḥ | adhva-bhiḥ | avyaḥ | vāre | pari | priyaḥ | sahasra-dhāraḥ | yāt | tanā

translation.original_ref: RV 9.52.3-5 (aṣṭaka 7, adhyāya 1, varga 9); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 687r
translation.original_text:
3ca̱rur na yas tam ī̍ṅkha̱yendo̱ na dāna̍m īṅkhaya | va̱dhair va̍dhasnav īṅkhaya ||
4ni śuṣma̍m indav eṣā̱m puru̍hūta̱ janā̍nām | yo a̱smām̐ ā̱dide̍śati ||
5śa̱taṁ na̍ inda ū̱tibhi̍ḥ sa̱hasra̍ṁ vā̱ śucī̍nām | pava̍sva maṁha̱yadra̍yiḥ ||
translation.text:
3Him who is like a caldron shake: O Indu, shake thy gift to us Shake it, armed Warrior! with thine arms.
4Indu, invoked with many a prayer, bring down the vigour of these men, Of him who threatens us with war.
5Indu, Wealth-giver, with thine help pour out for us a hundred, yea, A thousand of thy pure bright streams.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 687r (numbered 4r by the scribe) (OPenn image 687, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.52.3 ‹-itivadha-sno īṅkhaya›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 687v (numbered 4v by the scribe), begins in RV 9.54.4 ‹iti indra-yuḥ›. Verses 9.52.3-5 end on this page; 9.52.3 begins on fol. 686v (numbered 3v by the scribe).
translation.edition_text:
3caruḥ | na | yaḥ | tam | īṅkhaya | indo iti | na | dānam | īṅkhaya | vadhaiḥ | vadhasno itivadha-sno | īṅkhaya
4ni | śuṣmam | indo iti | eṣām | puru-hūta | janānām | yaḥ | asmān | ādideśati
5śatam | naḥ | indo iti | ūti-bhiḥ | sahasram | vā | śucīṇām | pavasva | maṃhayat-rayiḥ
